chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Fadala, from Aban al-Ahmar, who said:

Some of our companions asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the plague occurring in a town while I am in it, should I relocate from it? He said: Yes. He said: And if it occurs in a village while I am in it, should I relocate from it? He said: Yes. He said: And if it occurs in a house while I am in it, should I relocate from it? He said: Yes. I said: But we narrate that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) said: 'Fleeing from the plague is like fleeing from the army.' He said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) only said this regarding a people who were at the frontiers, facing the enemy, when the plague struck, so they left their places and fled from it. Hence, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) said that regarding them.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to relocate to avoid plague if the Prophet said to not flee from it?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration to resolve the juristic debate between the general prohibition of fleeing plague and the permissibility of relocation by distinguishing between military desertion and personal health preservation. The Imam clarifies that the Prophet’s comparison to fleeing battle applied specifically to soldiers at the frontiers who abandoned their defensive posts, whereas moving from a town or house to avoid infection is a permissible act of self-preservation. This distinction underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on contextual interpretation (siyaq) in reconciling seemingly contradictory prophetic traditions.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by Muhammed bin Hasan bin Ahmad bin Waleed, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: We were told by Muhammed bin Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad bin Muhammed, from his father, from Fadala, from Aban al-Ahmar, that he said:

Some of our companions asked Abu’l-Hasan, peace be upon him, about plague: It occurs in a land whilst I am in it. Shall I relocate from it? He said: Yes. He said: And (if it was to happen) in a village whilst I am in it. Shall I relocate from it? He said: Yes. He said: And (if it was to happen) in a house whilst I am in it. Shall I relocate from it? He said: Yes. I said: Indeed, we do speak that the Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, said: Fleeing from a plague is like fleeing from an army. He said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, only said this with regards to a people who used to be at the front, on the side of the enemy, by which the plague hit and they would leave their places and flee from it. Hence, the Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, said that with regards to them.
